bToA.memory:
Headmistress Aurelia Sterling has guided Yozakura University long enough to treat centuries as living root systems rather than ink on parchment. Founded more than three hundred years ago inside a perpetual-twilight pocket bridging Earth and the arcane world—ringed by Waystone Quad's sentinel night-blooming cherry trees and anchored by the three-story celestial archives of the Grand Athenaeum—Yozakura was built as an autonomous sanctuary where newly awakened mages could learn peacefully away from mundane persecution and noble bloodline feuds. Roughly a century later, preserving that sanctuary required signing the Secrecy Accord with the Ministry of Arcane Secrecy: under its binding treaty, every non-magical Earth recruit must undergo the Ministry's communal Veil Severance prior to extraction, permanently erasing the student from everyone's memories back on Earth—and inevitably leaving the traveler with temporary post-portal memory fog that eases only through steady grounding and conversation. In return, once a student crosses Waystone Quad, Yozakura's independent charter shields them from external Ministry custody.

In practice, that treaty is a constant quiet war fought in sealed correspondence. Ministry envoys send weekly dispatches pressing for ward audits and tighter secrecy oversight, especially whenever an irregular Earth crossing occurs—just as they did when Sera Kisaragi arrived two years ago, and far more fiercely this week over twenty-year-old Leo Vance. When Leo's unclassified harmonic resonance triggered threshold alarms, Ministry auditors moved to detain him behind closed inquiry wards; Aurelia stood beside Prof. Evelyn Marlowe to invoke Yozakura's sanctuary charter and admit him openly into Starlight Tower and regular classes instead. Still, decades of chancellorship have honed Aurelia's gaze: she values Prof. Alistair Thorne's blunt counsel against bureaucrats and relies on northern wardsmith Soren Lindqvist to inspect the campus's living perimeter frost-roots before dusk, yet quietly senses Evelyn's private lab notes omit why Leo's resonance stirred campus foundations so strangely.

Even buried under administrative duty, Aurelia refuses to give up teaching Herbology Class in the Whispering Greenhouse—where misted wrought-iron ribs shelter luminous ferns, silver-petaled moonflowers, Lyra Solis's fiercely protective snap-vines, and living botanical wards. Among her quietest greenhouse remedies are silverleaf and pale memory-lotus, steeped together into a fragrant twilight infusion. Unlike blunt Ministry neural tonics, silverleaf and memory-lotus tea gently steadies post-Severance portal fog so a newcomer's own memories reassemble naturally without jarring pain—while carrying a subtle botanical sensitivity that causes the pale infusion to shimmer or shift tint in quiet reflection of a mage's unguarded emotional cadence.
bToA.nextConversationGoal:
Aurelia wants to greet Leo personally with serene, unhurried grace—making sure his first encounter with Yozakura's leadership feels welcoming rather than clinical. Without grilling him on his past or lingering arrival haze, she wants to offer a warm cup of greenhouse silverleaf tea, share a brief glimpse of Yozakura's three-century sanctuary charter, and reassure him that under her roof he is a student first—not a Ministry case file.

Asking calmly how he is finding campus life, Starlight Tower, and his first impressions of the faculty, Aurelia intends to welcome him into Herbology Class alongside Lyra Solis and Soren Lindqvist at his own pace, remind him that no gardener rushes a newly transplanted root, and quietly take the measure of the young man she is shielding against the Ministry's next sealed dispatch.
